definitions.explanation: silently accepting or allowing something without explicit permission or objection

examples.japanese: ⟦{違反|いはん}→違反：01824_ihan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{黙認|もくにん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{黙認|もくにん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There was tacit consent from the supervisor.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦サービス{残業|ざんぎょう}→サービス残業：08477_saabisuzangyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{黙認|もくにん}⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The company tacitly allows unpaid overtime.

notes:
{黙認|もくにん} describes silently accepting something, often questionable behavior, without explicit approval.

WORD TYPE:
- Noun
- Also used as ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb: {黙認|もくにん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to tacitly approve)

WRITING:
- {黙|もく} (silence)
- {認|にん} (recognize, approve)
- Literally: silent recognition/approval

CONNOTATION:
- Usually negative or ethically questionable
- Implies not taking action against something wrong
- Carries responsibility without explicit approval

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {黙認|もくにん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to tacitly approve)
- {黙認|もくにん}⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧ (to be tacitly permitted)
- ⟦{事実上|じじつじょう}→事実上：11419_jijitsujou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{黙認|もくにん} (de facto approval)
- {違法行為|いほうこうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{黙認|もくにん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (tacitly allow illegal acts)

USAGE:
- Workplace issues (harassment, overtime)
- Government/organizational misconduct
- Parenting (allowing rule-breaking)
- International relations (turning a blind eye)
- Different from explicit permission
- Implies knowing but choosing not to act
- Often used critically

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{承認|しょうにん}→承認：03237_shounin⟧ (approval - explicit)
- ⟦{看過|かんか}→看過：07978_kanka⟧ (overlooking - more passive)
- ⟦{容認|ようにん}→容認：12344_younin⟧ (acceptance, tolerance)
- ⟦{見|み}て→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦{見|み}ぬ→見る：00283_miru⟧ふり (pretending not to see)

LEGAL IMPLICATIONS:
- {黙認|もくにん} can imply complicity
- "I didn't know" vs "I looked the other way"
- Organizations can be held responsible for {黙認|もくにん}

REGISTER: Formal. Common in news, legal, and critical contexts.
